overall: The AG found one violation: the Board failed to approve March 28 open session minutes in a timely manner. Other allegations on executive session purpose, notice posting, notice specificity, and intent were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to create and approve minutes of its March 28 open session in a timely manner.
Complaint did not distinguish open and executive session minutes; to the extent it challenged timing of March 28 executive session minutes, the AG addressed the standard.
allegations.key_passage: we do not require that a public body approve executive session minutes within three meetings or 30 days, only that they be “create[d] and maintain[ed]” and “review[ed]” “at reasonable intervals” to determine whether continued nondisclosure is warranted.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board met in executive session on March 28 under Purpose 6 without a proper purpose, to discuss the lease of 158 Center Hill Road.
allegations.key_passage: Similarly, here, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it discussed 158 Center Hill Rd. in executive session under Purpose 6.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 28 meeting notice was not properly posted on the Board section of the website; the AG found the complaint timely and posting compliant.
allegations.key_passage: Access to the meeting notice through the agenda center, as described above, satisfies the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to announce upon returning to open session that it had met in executive session on March 28.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review allegations that the Board failed to make an open session announcement that it had met in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 16 executive session notice listing '30 Town Wharf (Lease)' under Purpose 6 was insufficiently specific.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the description “30 Town Wharf (Lease),” in the context of a proper executive session under Purpose 6, satisfied the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the minutes delay was an intentional violation; the AG declined to find intent.
allegations.key_passage: However, as those determinations were issued after March 28, we do not find that the Board acted intentionally in delaying approval of the minutes of the March 28 meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
